Before any delegation arrives, I check three things. First, the visas. Some visitors have to apply for a visa, and the paperwork can take weeks, so I send the list of requirements on the first day. Second, the budget. Our director has to approve it before I can sign any contract. And third, the venue. I always have a backup plan, because a hotel once cancelled one week before an event. That was a terrible week. I also tell the visitors clearly what is mandatory and what is optional. Registration is mandatory. The city tour and the dinner are optional. They do not have to come, but most people do.

A few years ago, we had a booth at a trade fair in Canada. Everything was ready: the products, the booth, the flights. Then, four days before the fair, someone from the organization called us. We had forgotten a form. Every exhibitor had to send it, because it was about safety. It was mandatory. It was urgent, and we spent two nights doing the paperwork. In the end, they approved it, but it was very close. Now my team has a simple rule. On the first day of any project, we make a list of all the requirements, and we check it every week. It sounds boring, but it works.
